questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Indefinite Integral of a Rational Function Using Partial Fractions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
3{x}^{2}+x=x(3x+1).
$$

We convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x(3x+1)} & =\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(3x+1)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
2=A(3x+1)+Bx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A(3(-\frac{1}{3})+1)+B(-\frac{1}{3}) \\ 2 & =-\frac{1}{3}B \\ 6 & =-B \\ B & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A(3(0)+1)+B(0) \\ 2 & =A\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x(3x+1)}=\frac{2}{x}-\frac{6}{3x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x(3x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}-\frac{6}{3x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{3}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\int \frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)}\,\text{d}x=a\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+b\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C,
$$

find the value of $a+b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)} & =\frac{A}{3x+2}+\frac{B}{2x-3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
13=A(2x-3)+B(3x+2).
$$

Plugging in $x=\frac{3}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =A(2(\frac{3}{2})-3)+B(3(\frac{3}{2})+2) \\ 13 & =\frac{13}{2}B \\ B & =2\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-\frac{2}{3},$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =A(2(-\frac{2}{3})-3)+B(3(-\frac{2}{3})+2) \\ 13 & =-\frac{13}{3}A \\ A & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)}=-\frac{3}{3x+2}+\frac{2}{2x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{3}{3x+2}+\frac{2}{2x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{3}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=1,b=-1,$ and $a+b=1-1=0.$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following indefinite integral and fill in the missing coefficients.

$\int \frac{11}{(2x+5)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}$\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+5|\,+\,$
{{field-2}}$\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+C$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
(2x+5)(x-2).
$$

We convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11}{(2x+5)(x-2)} & =\frac{A}{2x+5}+\frac{B}{x-2},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
11=A(x-2)+B(2x+5).
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =9B \\ B & =\frac{11}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-\frac{5}{2},$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =-\frac{9}{2}A \\ A & =-\frac{22}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{11}{(2x+5)(x-2)}=-\frac{22}{9(2x+5)}+\frac{11}{9(x-2)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{11}{(2x+5)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{22}{9}\int \frac{1}{2x+5}\,\text{d}x+\frac{11}{9}\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{11}{9}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+5|+\frac{11}{9}\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following indefinite integral and fill in the missing coefficients.

$\int \frac{7x-11}{(x-8)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}$\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-8|\,+\,$
{{field-2}}$\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
(x-8)(x+1).
$$

We convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7x-11}{(x-8)(x+1)} & =\frac{A}{x-8}+\frac{B}{x+1},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
7x-11=A(x+1)+B(x-8).
$$

Plugging in $x=8,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7(8)-11 & =A(8+1)+B(8-8) \\ 45 & =9A \\ A & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7(-1)-11 & =A(-1+1)+B(-1-8) \\ -18 & =-9B \\ B & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{7x-11}{(x-8)(x+1)}=\frac{5}{x-8}+\frac{2}{x+1}.
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{7x-11}{(x-8)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{1}{x-8}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-8|+2\,\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\int \frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}\,\text{d}x=a\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+b\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+C,
$$

find the value of $a+b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)} & =\frac{A}{x-3}+\frac{B}{2x+1},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
5x-1=A(2x+1)+B(x-3).
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-\frac{1}{2})-1 & =A(2(-\frac{1}{2})+1)+B(-\frac{1}{2}-3) \\ -\frac{7}{2} & =-\frac{7}{2}B \\ B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(3)-1 & =A(2(3)+1)+B(3-3) \\ 14 & =7A \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}=\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{2x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{2x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=2,b=\frac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=2+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2}.$

questions.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
{x}^{2}+4x-5=(x+5)(x-1).
$$

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-1}{{x}^{2}+4x-5} & =\frac{5x-1}{(x+5)(x-1)}=\frac{A}{x+5}+\frac{B}{x-1},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
5x-1=A(x-1)+B(x+5).
$$

Plugging in $x=1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(1)-1 & =A(1-1)+B(1+5) \\ 4 & =6B \\ B & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-5,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-5)-1 & =A(-5-1)+B(-5+5) \\ -26 & =-6A \\ A & =\frac{13}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5x-1}{{x}^{2}+4x-5}=\frac{13}{3(x+5)}+\frac{2}{3(x-1)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x-1}{{x}^{2}+4x-5}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{13}{3(x+5)}+\frac{2}{3(x-1)})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+5|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x-1}{{x}^{2}+4x-5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+5|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{0}\frac{5x-1}{{x}^{2}+4x-5}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+5|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|]}_{-4}^{0} \\  & =(\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))-(\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) \\  & =\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\  & =\frac{11}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that a denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
12{x}^{2}-x-6=(4x-3)(3x+2).
$$

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{36x-10}{12{x}^{2}-x-6} & =\frac{36x-10}{(4x-3)(3x+2)}=\frac{A}{4x-3}+\frac{B}{3x+2},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
36x-10=A(3x+2)+B(4x-3).
$$

Plugging in $x=\frac{3}{4},$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}36(\frac{3}{4})-10 & =A(3(\frac{3}{4})+2)+B(4(\frac{3}{4})-3) \\ 17 & =\frac{17}{4}A \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-\frac{2}{3},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}36(-\frac{2}{3})-10 & =A(3(-\frac{2}{3})+2)+B(4(-\frac{2}{3})-3) \\ -34 & =-\frac{17}{3}B \\ B & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{36x-10}{12{x}^{2}-x-6}=\frac{4}{4x-3}+\frac{6}{3x+2}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{36x-10}{12{x}^{2}-x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4}{4x-3}+\frac{6}{3x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x-3|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{36x-10}{12{x}^{2}-x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x-3|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(4x-3)(3x+2)^{2}|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{36x-10}{12{x}^{2}-x-6}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(4x-3)(3x+2)^{2}|{|}_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{49}{4})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(12) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{49}{48}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{49}{48}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that a denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
5{x}^{2}-19x-4=(5x+1)(x-4).
$$

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{15x-39}{5{x}^{2}-19x-4} & =\frac{15x-39}{(5x+1)(x-4)}=\frac{A}{5x+1}+\frac{B}{x-4},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
15x-39=A(x-4)+B(5x+1).
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}15(4)-39 & =A(4-4)+B(5(4)+1) \\ 21 & =21B \\ B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{5},$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}15(-\frac{1}{5})-39 & =A(-\frac{1}{5}-4)+B(5(-\frac{1}{5})+1) \\ -42 & =-\frac{21}{5}A \\ A & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{15x-39}{5{x}^{2}-19x-4}=\frac{10}{5x+1}+\frac{1}{x-4}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15x-39}{5{x}^{2}-19x-4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{10}{5x+1}+\frac{1}{x-4})\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x+1|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15x-39}{5{x}^{2}-19x-4}\,\text{d}x & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x+1|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(5x+1)^{2}(x-4)|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{15x-39}{5{x}^{2}-19x-4}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(5x+1)^{2}(x-4)|{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(242)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{242}{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{121}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x+29}{(x+7)(x+4)}=\frac{A}{(x+7)}+\frac{B}{(x+4)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
5x+29=A(x+4)+B(x+7).
$$

Plugging in $x=-4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-4)+29 & =A(-4+4)+B(-4+7) \\ 9 & =3B \\ B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-7,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-7)+29 & =A(-7+4)+B(-7+7) \\ -6 & =-3A \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5x+29}{(x+7)(x+4)}=\frac{2}{(x+7)}+\frac{3}{(x+4)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x+29}{(x+7)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x+7}+\frac{3}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x+7}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+7|+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+7)^{2}|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+4)^{3}|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+7)^{2}(x+4)^{3}|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x+29}{(x+7)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+7)^{2}|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+4)^{3}|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+7)^{2}(x+4)^{3}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{-5}\frac{5x+29}{(x+7)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+7)^{2}(x+4)^{3}|{|}_{-6}^{-5} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{3}) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)} & =\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
x+1=A(x+3)+Bx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+1 & =A(-3+3)+B(-3) \\ -2 & =-3B \\ B & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+1 & =A(0+3)+B(0) \\ 1 & =3A \\ A & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}=\frac{1}{3x}+\frac{2}{3(x+3)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{3x}+\frac{2}{3(x+3)})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\frac{2}{3}\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x(x+3)^{2}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x(x+3)^{2}|{|}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x^2+3x-4 = (x-1)(x+4) \,.
$$

So, the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4} & =\frac{5x}{(x-1)(x+4)} \\  & =\frac{A}{(x-1)}+\frac{B}{(x+4)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & =A(x+4)+B(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-4) & =A(-4+4)+B(-4-1) \\ -20 & =-5B \\ B & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, by plugging in $x=1,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(1) & =A(1+4)+B(1-1) \\ 5 & =5A \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{5x}{x^2+3x-4}  = \dfrac{1}{(x-1)} +\dfrac{4}{(x+4)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4}\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{4}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\text{d}x+4\int \frac{1}{x+4}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that a denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
4x^2-1 = (2x+1)(2x-1) \,.
$$

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3}{4{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{2x+3}{(2x+1)(2x-1)} \\  & =\frac{A}{(2x+1)}+\frac{B}{(2x-1)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =A(2x-1)+B(2x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=\dfrac{1}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(\frac{1}{2})+3 & =A(2(\frac{1}{2})-1)+B(2(\frac{1}{2})+1) \\ 4 & =2B \\ B & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-\dfrac{1}{2},$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-\frac{1}{2})+3 & =A(2(-\frac{1}{2})-1)+B(2(-\frac{1}{2})+1) \\ 2 & =-2A \\ A & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{4x^2-1} = -\dfrac{1}{(2x+1)} +\dfrac{2}{(2x-1)}.
$$

Now, we integrate and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{4{x}^{2}-1}\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{1}{(2x+1)}+\frac{2}{(2x-1)})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{1}{2x+1}\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{2x-1}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+2(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|)+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{4{x}^{2}-1}\text{d}x & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-1|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{2x-1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{2x+3}{4{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡{|\frac{2x-1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{7}{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{7}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
